commercial_incentive: none evident; offers a free Discord server/email for questions rather than a paid service
key_insights: Scored a 35 composite ACT (described as 'suboptimal' by the speaker) but with 36s on math and science, which he felt was sufficient given his STEM focus.
Took the maximum STEM APs his school allowed, then added college-level courses (differential equations, linear algebra, group theory) once AP options ran out, to keep maximizing rigor.

Notes MIT's application has unique sections not found on the standard Common App: separate fields for jobs, summer activities, and up to five scholastic plus five non-scholastic awards, which let him include more material than a typical application format allows.

His top-billed activity was a self-founded nonprofit that raised about $10,000 and 1,000+ donated books; his second was 3 years in an NLP research lab producing multiple papers (2 published, 1 in progress at time of application).

Submitted MIT's optional maker portfolio and a research supplement with detailed project write-ups (EEG headset, drone, robotics team) and credits the maker portfolio specifically as the piece he believes sealed his admission.

Advises prospective applicants to go deep into one specific subject/skill area (citing Olympiad-level depth as a common trait among MIT peers) rather than spreading effort broadly across many activities.
